steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Texture describes how musical lines combine: monophonic (single line), homophonic (melody + chords), polyphonic (independent lines), antiphonal (spatially separated groups).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Sonority (timbre) is the unique sound quality of each instrument or voice — same notes sound different on violin vs clarinet vs voice.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Dynamics shape musical expression: crescendo builds intensity; diminuendo releases it; sudden changes (sfz) create drama and surprise.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Instrumental techniques change sonority: arco (bowed) vs pizzicato (plucked) on strings; con sordino (muted) brass; palm mute on guitar; falsetto voice.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Describe how dynamics texture and sonority are used in a piece of music you have studied. Use musical vocabulary. | Compare how two different pieces use dynamics texture and sonority. Explain the effect in each case. | How could you use dynamics texture and sonority in your own composition or performance? Explain your choices.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A detailed description using precise musical vocabulary (e.g. specific terms from the AQA elements list), referencing a named piece with accurate observations about how the elements are used and their | A comparison of two pieces identifying similarities and differences in how dynamics texture and sonority are used, explaining the different effects created in each musical context, using comparative l | A practical application showing understanding of how dynamics texture and sonority can be manipulated in composition or performance, with specific examples of choices made and their intended effect.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always use PRECISE musical vocabulary — not vague descriptions like it sounds nice Reference SPECIFIC musical elements when analysing any piece For listening questions: identify elements FIRST, then explain their effect For study pieces: know the context, structure and key features in detail For performing: focus on accuracy, expression and interpretation For composing: show development of ideas, not just repetition
